assumptions: Customer raw site records are accessed only with explicit authorization, while retained derived records are limited to rights granted in signed contracts.
Qualified engineers remain responsible for site-specific approval and can be sourced from multiple providers rather than one indispensable partner.
Hardware and installation remain customer-direct or pass-through, so the operating company does not assume speculative inventory exposure.
A 5 million PLN founder-net-worth path would require repeatable multi-region portfolio revenue or licensable workflow economics; local one-off consulting alone is assumed insufficient.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid engagements from independent commercial owners showing realized price, delivery hours, engineer and insurance cost, contribution margin, acquisition cost and payback; measured decision-time or avoided-rework improvement versus incumbent routes; conversion to executed projects; paid refresh or additional-site purchases; signed data-rights terms; and repeatable referrals from more than the family relationship.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Owners of aging PV systems can face a costly decision gap between a fault or support expiry and a technically compliant repair or repowering path. Turning fragmented site, equipment, certification, quote, and engineering information into an auditable pre-failure decision record is useful, though it is an operational improvement more than a uniquely protected insight.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: The packet evidences paid diagnostics, maintenance, parts obligations, and modernization, so the underlying loss and budget owners are credible. It does not establish willingness to pay a separate independent readiness fee before failure, a repeat refresh, or a project-management fee rather than buying the same work from an incumbent OEM, installer, engineer, or O&M provider.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Prepaid bounded dossiers, milestone-funded projects, customer-direct hardware, and a 20,000 PLN launch budget produce much better cash conversion and downside control than a hardware-heavy service. Attractive economics remain uncertain because pricing, labor per dossier, engineer review, referrals, insurance, revisions, support, CAC, conversion to projects, and repeat demand are unmeasured; without productization or recurring portfolio work, owner earnings may resemble a small consultancy rather than a compounding asset.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Post-warranty, unsupported, or operationally critical commercial PV sites are a reasonably focused beachhead with identifiable asset and O&M budget owners. The reachable account count and frequency of unresolved decisions are unknown after excluding sites with satisfactory OEM, warranty, installer, or routine repowering routes.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Vendor neutrality, portable evidence packs, and direct owner contracts could support a trusted niche position. However, OEMs, engineering firms, installers, and O&M providers already control many customer relationships and can bundle diagnosis, compatibility analysis, procurement, and project coordination, while the founder-owned workflow has no demonstrated outcome advantage.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A repeatable workflow could expand across portfolios, inverter families, regions, compliance refreshes, procurement, and eventually licensing to independent O&M providers. The path depends on standardizing heterogeneous site work and obtaining repeatable data rights and outcomes; otherwise expansion adds consulting labor rather than operating leverage.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Company-owned software, schemas, and contractually permitted derived outcome records are controllable and potentially cumulative. They are not yet a moat: customers may refuse useful data rights, records may remain sparse and site-specific, and incumbents can implement similar document and decision workflows using their installed relationships and proprietary equipment knowledge.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: An independent, auditable, multi-vendor decision pack could reduce search time, emergency rework, and dependence on a single seller. No measured improvement in decision speed, cost, accuracy, procurement outcome, or downtime is shown, and qualified site-specific engineering remains mandatory, limiting the degree of automation and differentiation.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The installed PV fleet is expanding and aging, while certification changes and modernization spending increase the value of documented, current replacement decisions. Momentum also benefits incumbent repowering providers, so the timing supports the problem category but not necessarily this independent intermediary.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: A consenting pilot through the family installer is credible, and nonexclusive installer/O&M referrals plus direct portfolio sales are sensible routes. The model still lacks signed channels, direct account conversion, measured acquisition cost, and proof that referrers will send valuable work instead of bundling it, while direct B2B selling may demand more founder time and social energy than planned.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The analytical and document-normalization work fits the founder's skills, AI leverage, low capital preference, and five-hour daily limit, and field execution can be contracted. Material risks remain around incomplete customer records, professional liability, the boundary between analysis and engineering approval, current certification, contractor capacity, cybersecurity, and maintaining a clear non-guarantee when no safe recommendation is available.

highest_value_structural_change: Convert the one-off dossier into a standardized prepaid portfolio contract with explicit decision-time service levels, scheduled paid refresh triggers, portable outputs, narrowly defined derived-data rights, and a replaceable engineer network, then license or embed the proven workflow through independent O&M channels while retaining direct contractual ownership of the service account.
main_structural_strength: The design is a prepaid, bounded, founder-controlled analytical workflow with qualified engineering review and customer-direct hardware, making it testable alongside employment with limited capital exposure.
primary_score_limiter: The deliverable is readily bundled by firms that already own the service relationship, while neither separate willingness to pay nor a durable advantage from the workflow and derived records is established; this leaves a credible service wedge but a weak demonstrated path to high-margin scale and 5 million PLN of founder net worth.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: SolarEdge and SMA already offer rapid replacement or repowering paths through established channels, and the technical evidence shows that replacement remains site-specific and engineering-intensive, directly limiting both the independent wedge and software-like standardization.
